chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The believer is tried with every trial and dies with every (type of) death, except that he does not kill himself.'

key_terms.بَلِيَّة: Trial, affliction, ordeal; any misfortune or tribulation sent as a test
key_terms.مِيتَة: A (type of) death, manner of dying — encompasses all natural and accidental deaths
key_terms.يَقْتُلُ نَفْسَهُ: Kills himself — prohibited self-destruction; suicide is the sole excluded exception
key_terms.يُبْتَلَى: Is tried, tested, afflicted — from the root b-l-w, indicating divinely ordained trial

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about trials and the prohibition of suicide?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) teaches that a true believer may be subjected to all manner of afflictions and all forms of death — illness, accident, natural calamity — yet one boundary remains inviolable: a believer never takes his own life. This hadith frames tribulation as a divinely ordained test and sharply distinguishes natural death (however it comes) from self-destruction, which is absolutely forbidden. In the context of early Islamic jurisprudence and theology, this teaching reinforced both the sanctity of life and the believer's patient acceptance of whatever trials God decrees.
